skill.name: add-dependency
skill.description: Add a third-party Gradle dependency through approval, stable version research, version catalog updates, and build verification.
skill.summary: Manage new Gradle dependencies with approval and version catalog consistency.
skill.author: AnySoftKeyboard

content.value_statement: Adding libraries without review can create version drift and unnecessary maintenance. This skill guides approval, version discovery, catalog updates, and build verification.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates whether a third-party dependency is necessary before modifying project files.
Requires user approval and explains why alternatives were not selected.
Directs a web search for the latest stable library version.
Adds version and library entries to the Gradle version catalog.
Runs a relevant Gradle build task to verify dependency resolution.
limitations: Designed for Gradle projects that use a version catalog.
Does not perform license, vulnerability, or supply-chain analysis.
Requires web access to verify the current stable version.
Cannot guarantee compatibility beyond results from the selected build task.

use_cases.title: Add an Android Library
use_cases.description: Introduce a stable Android library through the shared version catalog and verify the affected build.

use_cases.title: Review a Dependency Proposal
use_cases.description: Compare a proposed library with existing solutions before approving repository changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Automated Changes
use_cases.description: Guide an AI coding tool through a consistent approval and verification process.

prompt_templates.title: Add One Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [library] to this Gradle project. Explain why it is needed and ask for approval before changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one dependency added safely.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alternatives
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [library] against [alternative]. Recommend whether to add it, verify the latest stable version, then wait for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants evidence before selecting a library.

prompt_templates.title: Update the Version Catalog
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [group]:[artifact] through gradle/libs.versions.toml after approval. Use clear aliases, then run the relevant Gradle build task.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs a catalog-compliant dependency change.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Implement
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this dependency for necessity, maintenance, compatibility, and catalog consistency. Compare alternatives, obtain approval, implement it, and verify the affected build.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a complete dependency decision and implementation workflow.

output_examples.input: Add Retrofit for a new HTTP API client.
output: Retrofit is justified for typed HTTP APIs, while the current project lacks equivalent networking support.
Approval is requested before any repository files are changed.
After approval, the stable version and library alias are added to the catalog, followed by build verification.

output_examples.input: Add WorkManager and verify the Android application build.
output: Existing scheduling options are reviewed before recommending WorkManager.
The current stable release is confirmed, then the version catalog is updated after approval.
The relevant Android build completes and the dependency resolves successfully.

best_practices: Confirm the dependency is necessary and discuss alternatives before requesting approval.
Verify the stable version from authoritative sources because search results can be stale.
Run the narrowest relevant Gradle task after updating the version catalog.
anti_patterns: Do not edit project files before explicit approval unless autonomous changes were already approved.
Do not hardcode dependency versions in Gradle build files.
Do not select prerelease or dynamic versions when a stable release is required.

faq.question: Does this skill add dependencies without approval?
faq.answer: No. It requests user approval before modifying files unless autonomous changes were already approved.

faq.question: Which projects are supported?
faq.answer: It targets Gradle projects that manage dependencies through gradle/libs.versions.toml.

faq.question: How does it choose a version?
faq.answer: It directs a web search for the latest stable version before updating the catalog.

faq.question: Does it check dependency security?
faq.answer: No. License, vulnerability, provenance, and supply-chain checks require separate tools or review.

faq.question: How is the change verified?
faq.answer: It runs a relevant Gradle build or sync task and checks whether dependency resolution succeeds.

faq.question: Can it place versions in build.gradle.kts?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires versions and library aliases in the shared version catalog.
